issue_context.body:
* [MySQL :: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual :: 6.2.15 Password Management - Password Expiration Policy](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/password-management.html#password-expiration-policy)
* [MySQL :: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual :: 6.2.16 Server Handling of Expired Passwords](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/expired-password-handling.html)
* [MySQL :: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual :: 13.7.1.3 CREATE USER Statement - Password Management Options](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/create-user.html#create-user-password-management)

review_comments: I don't get what is a sandbox mode at the first sight. Explain more, and probably rename it to something like `ExpiredPasswordMode` or so.

`Sandbox Mode` is a [term](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/expired-password-handling.html) from mysql. `InSandBoxMode` indicates that current session can only execute `set password` and `alter user` statements to reset the password.
Then maybe reference the link to the code instead of in the issue only.
Is there any reason we introduce this configuration? I see that sysvar @@disconnect_on_expired_password is added.
The sysvar @@disconnect_on_expired_password is read-only, the `disconnect-on-expired-password` configuration and command line option are used to set the sysvar
